title: Quadrilaterals: Parallelograms and the Mid-point Theorem
seo_title: Quadrilaterals Class 9 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 8)
standard_text: The diagonal divides a parallelogram into two congruent triangles; in a parallelogram opposite sides are equal and conversely; opposite angles are equal and conversely; a quadrilateral is a parallelogram if a pair of its opposite sides is parallel and equal; the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other and conversely; the Mid-point Theorem and its converse (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 9 Quadrilaterals worksheet (NCERT Chapter 8): angle sum, properties of parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses and squares, and the Mid-point Theorem. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Mid-point Theorem: DE ∥ BC and DE = ½ BC.
body_html:
How it works

The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°. In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal, opposite angles are equal, adjacent angles add up to 180°, and the diagonals bisect each other.

Rectangle: equal diagonals. Rhombus: diagonals bisect each other at right angles. Square: both.

Mid-point Theorem: the segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half of it. Converse: a line through the mid-point of one side, parallel to another side, bisects the third side.

Example

In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 70°. Find ∠B, ∠C and ∠D.

∠B = 180° − 70°

Opposite angles are equal

Answer: 110°, 70°, 110°

Example

D and E are the mid-points of AB and AC, and BC = 14 cm. Find DE.

DE = ½ BC

Answer: 7 cm

Common mistakes

  • Taking adjacent angles of a parallelogram as equal. They add up to 180°.
  • Thinking the diagonals of every parallelogram are equal. That is true only for rectangles (and squares).
  • Making DE equal to BC. The segment joining the mid-points is half of the third side.

faq.q: What are the properties of a parallelogram?
faq.a: Opposite sides are equal and parallel, opposite angles are equal, adjacent angles are supplementary, and the diagonals bisect each other.
The line segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half of it.

faq.q: How are the diagonals of a rhombus special?
faq.a: They bisect each other at right angles (and bisect the angles of the rhombus).

faq.q: What is the sum of the angles of a quadrilateral?
faq.a: 360°, because a diagonal divides it into two triangles of 180° each.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 84°, 97° and 51°. Find the fourth angle.
items.e: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°: 360° − 84° − 97° − 51° = 128°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB = 6x + 15 and CD = 3x + 24. Find AB.
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent: 6x + 15 = 3x + 24, so 3x = 9 and x = 3. AB = 33.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find x.
items.e: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary: x = 180 − 82 = 98.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB = 4x + 1 and CD = x + 10. Find AB.
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent: 4x + 1 = x + 10, so 3x = 9 and x = 3. AB = 13.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AE = 4x + 2 and EC = 2x + 12. Find AC.
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AE = EC: 4x + 2 = 2x + 12, so 2x = 10 and x = 5. AC = 2 × 22 = 44.

items.q: A rhombus has one side of length 19. What is its perimeter?
items.e: All four sides of a rhombus are congruent: 4 × 19 = 76.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus with diagonals meeting at E, and ∠ABE = 46°. Find ∠BAE.
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so ∠AEB = 90°. ∠BAE = 180 − 90 − 46 = 44°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle with diagonals meeting at E. AE = 2x − 4 and BD = x + 13. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so BD = AC = 2 × AE: x + 13 = 2(2x − 4), x = 7.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus with diagonals meeting at E, and ∠ABE = 33°. Find ∠BAE.
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so ∠AEB = 90°. ∠BAE = 180 − 90 − 33 = 57°.

items.q: The diagonals of a square meet at E. AE = 6. Find BD, and the measure of ∠AEB.
items.e: A square is a rectangle (congruent diagonals that bisect each other) and a rhombus (perpendicular diagonals). BD = 12 and ∠AEB = 90°.

items.q: The diagonals of a square meet at E. AE = 7. Find BD, and the measure of ∠AEB.
items.e: A square is a rectangle (congruent diagonals that bisect each other) and a rhombus (perpendicular diagonals). BD = 14 and ∠AEB = 90°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle with diagonals meeting at E. AE = 5x + 8 and BD = 3x + 37. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so BD = AC = 2 × AE: 3x + 37 = 2(5x + 8), x = 3.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle with diagonals meeting at E. AE = 4x + 2 and BD = 2x + 16. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so BD = AC = 2 × AE: 2x + 16 = 2(4x + 2), x = 2.

c: parallel to the third side and half of it

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus, and ∠BAC = 67°. Find ∠BAD.
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect its angles, so ∠BAD = 2 × 67° = 134°.

items.q: The diagonals of a square meet at E. AE = 8. Find BD, and the measure of ∠AEB.
items.e: A square is a rectangle (congruent diagonals that bisect each other) and a rhombus (perpendicular diagonals). BD = 16 and ∠AEB = 90°.

items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles: side = √(9² + 12²) = 15 cm.

items.q: The mid-points of the sides of a quadrilateral with diagonals 9 cm and 17 cm are joined. What is the perimeter of the new quadrilateral?
items.e: Each side of the new figure is half a diagonal (Mid-point Theorem), and each diagonal is used twice: 9 + 17 = 26 cm. It is a parallelogram.
